pages.p:
So far a variable held one value. An **array** holds a whole list of values in one variable. You write it with square brackets and put commas between the items.

«.length» tells you how many items the array has.
pages.tip: An array can hold numbers, text, true/false, or a mix. Most of the time all items are the same kind.

pages.p:
Each item has a position number called an **index**. The first item has index **0**, the second has index 1, and so on. You read an item with square brackets: «fruits[0]».

If you ask for an index that does not exist, you get «undefined».
pages.tip: An array with 3 items has indexes 0, 1 and 2. There is no index 3.

pages.p:
The last index is always «length - 1». So you can find the last item even when you do not know how long the array is.

You can also change an item: put the index on the left of «=».
pages.tip: «const» does not stop you changing the items. It only stops you from putting a different array in the variable.

pages.p:
«join» glues all the items into one piece of text. You choose the glue between the quotes. It is the easiest way to print an array in a clear way.

Two names can point to the **same** array. If you change it through one name, the other name sees the change too.
pages.tip: «const b = a» does not make a copy. It gives the same array a second name.

pages.p:
Arrays can grow and shrink. «push» adds an item to the **end**. «pop» removes the **last** item and gives it back to you.

Both change the array itself.
pages.tip: «push» adds many times in a row, like «list.push("x"); list.push("y");».

pages.p:
Two more methods work on the **front** of the array. «unshift» adds an item at the start. «shift» removes the first item and gives it back.

A tip to remember: «push/pop» work at the end, «unshift/shift» work at the start.
pages.o:
Zed Ana Bo
Zed
Ana Bo
pages.tip: Every item moves one place when you add or remove at the start. The indexes change.

pages.h: Build an array step by step
pages.p: A very common pattern: start with an empty array and push into it. Here we collect the first three square numbers.
pages.tip: Using «const» for an empty array that you fill later is fine and very common.

pages.h: A for loop over an array
pages.p:
Loops and arrays are best friends. Use the counter «i» as the index, and stop when «i» is smaller than «length». Then you visit every item once.

Use «<» and not «<=». Index «length» does not exist.
pages.tip: Read «i < nums.length» as: while there are items left.

pages.p:
When you only need the items and not their index, use **for...of**. On each round the variable holds the next item.

Read it as: for each name of the names.
pages.o:
Hello Ana
Hello Bo
Hello Cy
pages.tip: «const» works here because a fresh variable is made on each round.

pages.p:
«includes» answers yes or no with «true» or «false». «indexOf» gives the index of the item, or **-1** if it is not there.

The match must be exact, so capital letters matter.
pages.tip: Careful: «indexOf» can return 0 for a found item. Check «!== -1», not just the number.

pages.p:
«slice(start, end)» gives you a **new** array with the items from «start» up to, but **not including**, «end». The original array does not change.

With only one number, «slice» goes from there to the end.
pages.tip: You met «slice» on text in unit 2. On arrays it works the same way.

pages.p:
«split» cuts a text into an array. You say where to cut. «join» does the opposite and glues an array back into text.

This is great for words: «split(" ")» cuts at every space.
pages.tip: «split("")» with empty quotes cuts a text into single letters.

hand.why: Counting starts at 0, so index 1 is the second item, 20.

hand.q: Which index holds the first item of an array?
hand.why: Arrays start counting at 0. The last item is at «length - 1».
The array has 3 items. The last index is 3 - 1 = 2, which holds "blue".

hand.q: Fill in the method that adds "c" to the end.
hand.why: «push» adds an item at the end, so the array becomes a, b, c.
«pop» removes the 3. Then «push(9)» adds 9 at the end. The array is 1, 2, 9.

hand.q: Put the lines in order so it prints xy.
hand.why: You must create the array first, then push in the order x, y, and print at the end.

hand.q: Which method adds an item at the START of an array?
hand.why: «unshift» adds at the start. «shift» removes from the start, and «push» adds at the end.
«shift» removes and returns "x". Two items are left, so the text is "x" + 2 = "x2".

hand.q: Complete the loop that prints every name.
hand.why: «for (const n of names)» gives you each item of the array in turn.
«includes» answers with true or false. "c" is not in the array. The value -1 comes from «indexOf», not «includes».
«indexOf» gives the index, which is 2 for "c". For an item that is missing it gives -1.
Cutting at every space gives 3 words. Index 1 is the second word, "two".
«slice(1, 3)» starts at index 1 and stops before index 3. That gives the items 2 and 3.

hard.why: «b» is not a copy. It is the same array with a second name, so the push shows up in «a» too.
«slice» makes a new array and leaves the old one alone. «a» keeps 4 items and «b» gets 3.
After «shift» it is b, c. After «push» it is b, c, d. «unshift» puts e in front: e, b, c, d.
«big» starts at 3 and is replaced each time a bigger number appears: 8, then 9. Nothing beats 9.
Only the items at index 0 and index 3 are exactly "hi". "hello" and "hey" do not match.
The last index is 2. Index 3, which equals the length, does not exist. Reading it gives «undefined», not an error.

hard.q: Which loop header visits every index of arr exactly once?
hard.why: Start at 0 and stop before the length. «<=» goes one too far, starting at 1 skips the first item, and «length - 1» skips the last one.
Cutting at "-" gives "2024", "05" and "17". Joining index 1 and 2 as text gives "0517". The zero stays because they are texts, not numbers.
"x" is at index 0, and 0 is falsy, so the else part runs even though the item is there. Compare with «!== -1» instead.
The first «pop» gives 3 and the second gives 2. Together 3 + 2 is 5.

items.symptom: It prints NaN but the total should be 15.
items.why: With «<=» the loop also runs for index 3, which does not exist. Adding «undefined» to a number gives NaN. Use «<».

items.symptom: It prints undefined but it should print book.
items.why: The last index is «length - 1». Index «length» is one past the end.

items.symptom: It prints 5 but it should print 3.
items.why: «split("")» cuts between every character, commas included. To get the 3 letters, cut at the comma with «split(",")».

items.symptom: It prints Cy Ana Bo but the new member should come last.
items.why: «unshift» adds at the start. «push» adds at the end.

items.symptom: It prints 2,3 but it should print 2,3,4.
items.why: «slice» stops before the end index. To include the item at index 3, the end must be 4.

items.symptom: It prints false but "Cat" is in the list.
items.why: «includes» compares exactly, so "cat" and "Cat" are different. Use the same capital letter.

project.title: Word Wizard
project.brief:
Write a function «longestWord(sentence)» that returns the longest word in a sentence. Words are separated by a single space.

If two words are equally long, return the one that comes first.

Examples: «longestWord("I love coding")» is "coding" and «longestWord("The quick brown fox")» is "quick".

Hint: split the sentence, then loop and remember the best word so far.
